top_k_reconstruction.statement: S02 top_k_outlier_anchors store identity only (relative path, FNV content hash, block index, byte spans); they omit the observed value of every anchor. This review therefore reconstructs exactly one number per metric record: the observed metric maximum, taken from the metric record max field and bound to the first anchor in the record top_k list. The binding is justified by the descending insertion ordering contract (MetricAgg::observe retains an anchor only while value > last retained value; ties do not enter; the first retained anchor is therefore the maximum holder).
top_k_reconstruction.max_identification_rule: observed_max = metric record max; max_anchor = first top_k_outlier_anchors entry; every later anchor keeps identity only with reconstructed_value null (strictly below the previously retained value; exact value unknown).

gate_decisions.rationale: covering span never crosses blocks; structural range yields endpoint_pair=2 exactly; no arithmetic range enumeration; ContextRequest kinds closed; one worklist run; zero source mutation; zero prompt; provenance hops recorded. the observed maximum 504 lives in the KoAP-scale block npa/document_2001-12-30_195-fz block 542; the proposed 1024 keeps at least 2x headroom over the observed max and stays far below the quadratic pair-check danger zone. It is a revisable [proposed] safety ceiling with headroom, not a claim that larger legal structures do not exist; it is neither the observed max (504) nor a p999 histogram bucket edge (14). Raising it later requires a new review row; it is never lowered to an observed max or a bucket edge.
